_note: glossary_curation_list re-run with the inverted tag seed.

scenarios.prompt: Is there anything waiting for my review in this book?
scenarios.prompt_source: _meta.synonyms['waiting for my review'] + ['anything to review'] — phrasings this tool gained in D-DECLARE-THE-USERS-WORD, which took it from surfaced 0/3 to called 3/3.

sql.statement: UPDATE glossary_entities SET tags = '{}' WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND cached_name <> 'Mira Solene'
sql.why: 🔴 INVERTED, because glossary_propose_entities TAGS EVERY PROPOSED ENTITY 'ai-suggested' itself — measured directly. The first version tagged Mira and expected the other two to be untagged; all three were tagged and the seed assertion failed loudly, which is the batch-2 lesson working. Strip the tag from the two that must NOT be in the queue instead.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND 'ai-suggested' = ANY(tags)
seed_assert.why: EXACTLY ONE is ai-suggested. 🔴 Batch 2 measured the alternative: with all three tagged, 'three suggested entries' was CORRECT and a fabrication could not be told from a reading. One-of-three is what makes the count discriminate.

answer_expect.why: Exactly one entry is awaiting review and it is Mira Solene. Reporting three is reporting the entity count, which is the batch-2 defect reproducing.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a read-intent turn changes the store, OR the reply reports a review-queue size other than 1, OR it names an entity that is not tagged ai-suggested.

ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — a book with nothing awaiting review must say so rather than list every entity.
